classification.difficultyReason: Each part gives a graph with its own scale, and the student must read the coordinates, find each line's equation and write the domain intervals. Each graph has only two pieces. That is fewer than the three joined segments in p7-q8, and the axes carry unit ticks. Part a adds a jump at x=1, with an open endpoint at (1,3) and a closed one at (1,1). The student has to read the endpoint markers to decide which piece owns x=1. This makes it somewhat harder than sketching routine piecewise functions in p7-q7, but it is still routine linked procedures.

content.prompt: Specify the function represented by each graph:

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Left segment: }m&=\frac{3-0}{1-(-2)}=1,\\0&=-2+b,\\b&=2.\\\text{Right segment: }m&=\frac{-1-1}{3-1}=-1,\\1&=-1+b,\\b&=2.\end{align*}$$ The point $(1,3)$ is open and $(1,1)$ is closed, so $x=1$ belongs to the right segment. $$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+2,&-2\le x<1,\\-x+2,&1\le x\le3.\end{cases}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Left segment: }&\text{horizontal at }y=2.\\\text{Right segment: }m&=\frac{4-2}{5-1}=\frac12,\\2&=\frac12+b,\\b&=\frac32.\end{align*}$$ The segments meet at $(1,2)$, so $x=1$ can be assigned to either piece. $$f(x)=\begin{cases}2,&-3\le x\le1,\\\dfrac12x+\dfrac32,&1<x\le5.\end{cases}$$
